title: Prompt stewardship lifecycle: custodial rotation, soft-expiry TTLs, and config-triggered re-evals
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Our current canonical prompt bundles (golden promptsets) are effectively immutable but lack an operational lifecycle for custodial rotation, soft expirations, and automated re-evaluations when config or model variants change. Without a steward rotation and TTL mechanism, stale prompt bundles accumulate, permissions go out of date, and regression alerts are not consistently tied to the correct steward/contact.

Proposal summary: Implement a Prompt Stewardship Lifecycle service that attaches a steward identity, TTL (soft-expiry), and optional cryptographic signer to each canonical prompt bundle. When a prompt bundle approaches expiry or when an upstream configuration/model tag referenced by a bundle changes, the system will automatically spawn a re-eval job (delta/eval-orchestration) and notify the steward. Provide APIs for programmatic rotation, emergency handoff, and archival snapshots for reproducible regressions. Ensure RBAC integration with Console and audit logs for all steward/ownership transitions.
acceptance_criteria: Prompt bundle metadata is extended to include steward (principal id), soft_expiry_date, and signer_fingerprint fields
Create/Update API supports steward assignment and soft-expiry TTL (default 180 days) and returns immutable snapshot id on sign-off
When a referenced model/config tag used by a bundle is updated, a re-eval job is queued and visible in the eval orchestration dashboard within 5 minutes
Console shows steward, expiry, last-signed-by, and last-eval-result on the prompt bundle details page
Audit log entries are generated for steward change, TTL update, sign-off, and forced archival; logs retained per compliance settings
Automated email/slack notification to steward on expiry-30d, expiry-7d, and on any config-triggered re-eval failures
Migration from existing bundles to include a default steward and soft_expiry_date executed without downtime
Unit and integration tests cover API, RBAC checks, and re-eval trigger rules with >= 90% coverage for new modules
tasks: Design metadata schema changes and DB migration plan (prompt_bundles table)
Implement backend API endpoints: assign_steward, rotate_steward, sign_bundle, set_ttl, force_archive
Hook into config-change event bus to enqueue re-eval jobs with bundle snapshot references
Console UI: bundle detail card with steward, expiry, and quick-actions (rotate/sign/queue re-eval)
Integrate with existing eval-orchestration (ENG-41123) to pass prompt snapshot and config diffs
Add RBAC checks and audit events for steward operations (security review required)
Write migration script to populate steward/default TTL for orphan bundles and generate initial snapshots
Create rollout runbook and rollback steps for the migration and new APIs
Write end-to-end tests that simulate model/config change -> re-eval -> alert flow
notes: Default TTL proposed: 180 days (configurable per project). Soft-expiry means steward is notified and the bundle becomes read-only after expiry unless rotated.
Signed snapshots are optional but recommended for enterprise customers who need immutable provenance; use existing KMS integration for signing key management.
Aim to reuse existing event bus (config-change topic) to minimize infra churn; re-eval enqueuer should be idempotent.
We should avoid hard-deleting bundles: archival moves to read-only archive namespace and retains snapshot IDs for regression reproductions.
decisions: Use soft_expiry (notification + read-only) rather than forced deletion to minimize accidental loss of reference prompts
Assign default steward automatically to repo owner if none present during migration; allow HR/team lead override via Console
Trigger re-evals on model/config tag changes (exact-match or semantic bump) and on steward-initiated rotate events
Signed snapshots stored in S3 with signer fingerprint recorded in DB and optional public metadata manifest
migration_plan: Phase 1: Add columns (steward_id, soft_expiry_date, signer_fingerprint, snapshot_id) with null-safe defaults
Phase 2: Backfill steward_id from repository ownership and set soft_expiry_date = today + 180 days for existing bundles
Phase 3: Create initial signed snapshots for bundles that pass smoke evals (to avoid signing broken bundles)
Phase 4: Flip Console UI to show steward/expiry and restrict write actions for expired bundles
Rollback: Migration is additive; if issues arise, revert Console feature flag and abort background backfill jobs
rollout_plan: Gate backend changes behind feature flag (prompt-steward-lifecycle.v1)
Deploy backend and event-hook, run backfill on staging, validate smoke re-evals
Enable Console UI for internal teams for 2 weeks, gather feedback and fix UX issues
Open beta to select customers (enterprise) with signed snapshot option enabled
General availability after 4-week beta and security review sign-off
observability: Dashboards: per-project steward age distribution and expired-bundle trend
Audit logs: record who assigned/rotated steward and timestamp; integrate with Console audit search
